summary: This component renders a blog post card in one of two layouts—a small compact version or a larger default version. It takes a post object with details like title, description, and date, then displays them with proper formatting, localization, and image handling. The component handles different image paths depending on the layout and provides clickable links to the full post.

explanations.14: This interface defines the shape of a blog post object that the component expects to receive, including optional fields like description and mainTag.
explanations.28: This interface defines the props (inputs) that the PostCard component accepts, with sensible defaults for layout, defaultImage, and lazyImage.
explanations.35: The function signature destructures the props and provides default values: 'big' layout, a fallback image, and lazy loading enabled by default.
explanations.41: This unpacks all the post details from the post object so we can reference them easily throughout the component.
explanations.42: This hook pulls out the i18n object from Docusaurus context, which tells us what language/locale the user is currently viewing.
explanations.43: This formats the post's date string into a user-friendly display format based on the current locale.
explanations.44: This hook returns a function that converts tag names into properly localized label text.
explanations.52: This ensures the image path includes the correct locale prefix (like '/fr/') when needed; the comment explains why only the small layout needs this fix.
explanations.54: The component branches here: if the layout is 'small', it renders a compact card; otherwise it falls through to the default 'big' layout below.
explanations.70: This conditionally renders the counter text only if it exists, using the && operator to avoid rendering undefined values.
explanations.95: This checks if mainTag exists before rendering the tag link, preventing empty tag badges from appearing.
explanations.106: The aria-label uses the translate function to provide an accessible label that announces the article title when screen readers encounter this link.
explanations.117: This condition checks if there's anything to display in the metadata row (date or reading time) before rendering the paragraph container.
explanations.126: Math.ceil() rounds up the reading time to the nearest whole minute so users see '5 min read' instead of '4.7 min read'.
